sanskrit: karṇenābhyāhatā rājan pāñcālāḥ parameṣubhiḥ droṇena ca diśaḥ sarvā vīkṣamāṇāḥ pradudruvuḥ
english: Struck down by Karṇa's deadliest arrows, O king, and by Droṇa, the Pāñcālas fled in every direction, glancing all around them as they ran.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā svasainyaṃ prekṣya vidrutam apayāne matiṃ kṛtvā phalgunaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, seeing his own army routed, resolved upon retreat, and spoke these words to Phalguna.

sanskrit: paśya karṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ dhanuṣpāṇim avasthitam niśīthe dāruṇe kāle tapantam iva bhāskaram
english: Behold Karṇa, the mighty archer, standing firm with bow in hand in the terrible hour of midnight, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: karṇasāyakanunnānāṃ krośatām eṣa nisvanaḥ aniśaṃ śrūyate pārtha tvadbandhūnām anāthavat
english: Ceaselessly is heard, O Pārtha, the cry of your kinsmen pierced by Karṇa's shafts, wailing like men who have no protector.

sanskrit: yathā visṛjataś cāsya saṃdadhānasya cāśugān paśyāmi jayavikrāntaṃ kṣapayiṣyati no dhruvam
english: Seeing him nock and loose his swift arrows, victorious in his valor, I am certain he will surely destroy us.

sanskrit: yad atrānantaraṃ kāryaṃ prāptakālaṃ prapaśyasi karṇasya vadhasaṃyuktaṃ tat kuruṣva dhanaṃjaya
english: Whatever next deed you judge fit for this hour, one that will bring about the slaying of Karṇa—do it, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: evam ukto mahābāhuḥ pārthaḥ kṛṣṇam athābravīt bhītaḥ kuntīsuto rājā rādheyasyātivikramāt
english: Thus addressed, the mighty-armed Pārtha then spoke to Kṛṣṇa—for the king, the son of Kuntī, was filled with fear at the overwhelming valor of Rādheya.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate prāptakālaṃ karṇānīke punaḥ punaḥ bhavān vyavasyatāṃ kṣipraṃ dravate hi varūthinī
english: Matters being thus, let you decide quickly, again and again, what befits the hour against Karṇa's host—for the army is fleeing.

sanskrit: droṇasāyakanunnānāṃ bhagnānāṃ madhusūdana karṇena trāsyamānānām avasthānaṃ na vidyate
english: Of those broken and driven by Droṇa's arrows, O slayer of Madhu, and terrified by Karṇa, there is no holding their ground.

sanskrit: paśyāmi ca tathā karṇaṃ vicarantam abhītavat dravamāṇān rathodārān kirantaṃ viśikhaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: And I see Karṇa ranging without fear, showering the noble car-warriors as they flee with his sharp-pointed shafts.

sanskrit: naitad asyotsahe soḍhuṃ caritaṃ raṇamūrdhani pratyakṣaṃ vṛṣṇiśārdūla pādasparśam ivoragaḥ
english: I cannot bear to endure his exploits at the battle's front before my eyes, O tiger of the Vṛṣṇis, as a serpent cannot endure the touch of a foot.

sanskrit: sa bhavān atra yātvāśu yatra karṇo mahārathaḥ aham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmi māṃ vaiṣa madhusūdana
english: So let you drive swiftly to where Karṇa, the great car-warrior, stands: either I shall slay him, or he shall slay me, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca paśyāmi karṇaṃ kaunteya devarājam ivāhave vicarantaṃ naravyāghram atimānuṣavikramam
english: Vāsudeva said: I see Karṇa, O son of Kuntī, ranging in battle like the king of the gods—that tiger among men, of more than human valor.

sanskrit: naitasyānyo 'sti samare pratyudyātā dhanaṃjaya ṛte tvāṃ puruṣavyāghra rākṣasād vā ghaṭotkacāt
english: There is no other in this battle who can stand against him, O Dhanaṃjaya, save you, tiger among men, or the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: na tu tāvad ahaṃ manye prāptakālaṃ tavānagha samāgamaṃ mahābāho sūtaputreṇa saṃyuge
english: Yet I do not deem this the fitting hour, O sinless and mighty-armed one, for your encounter with the sūta's son in combat.

sanskrit: dīpyamānā maholkeva tiṣṭhaty asya hi vāsavī tvadarthaṃ hi mahābāho raudrarūpaṃ bibharti ca
english: For the dart of Vāsava abides with him, blazing like a great meteor, and it bears a dreadful form meant, O mighty-armed one, for you.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tu rādheyaṃ pratyudyātu mahābalaḥ sa hi bhīmena balinā jātaḥ suraparākramaḥ
english: Let mighty Ghaṭotkaca instead go forth against Rādheya, for he was begotten by the strong Bhīma, and his prowess is that of a god.

sanskrit: tasminn astrāṇi divyāni rākṣasāny āsurāṇi ca satataṃ cānurakto vo hitaiṣī ca ghaṭotkacaḥ vijeṣyati raṇe karṇam iti me nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: In him reside celestial weapons, and those of the rākṣasas and asuras; ever devoted to you and seeking your good is Ghaṭotkaca. He will conquer Karṇa in battle—of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā mahābāhuḥ pārthaṃ puṣkaralocanaḥ ājuhāvātha tad rakṣaḥ tac cāsīt prādur agrataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having so spoken to Pārtha, the mighty-armed, lotus-eyed one summoned that rākṣasa, and at once it appeared before them.

sanskrit: kavacī sa śarī khaḍgī sadhanvā ca viśāṃ pate abhivādya tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ ca dhanaṃjayam abravīt taṃ tadā hṛṣṭas tv ayam asmy anuśādhi mām
english: Armored, arrow-bearing, sword in hand and bow withal, O lord of peoples, he saluted Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya, and gladly said to him: Here I am—command me.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ meghasaṃkāśaṃ dīptāsyaṃ dīptakuṇḍalam abhyabhāṣata haiḍimbaṃ dāśārhaḥ prahasann iva
english: Then to that son of Hiḍimbā, cloud-hued, with blazing face and blazing earrings, the Dāśārha spoke, smiling the while.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaca vijānīhi yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi putraka prāpto vikramakālo 'yaṃ tava nānyasya kasya cit
english: Ghaṭotkaca, mark well what I shall tell you, my son: the hour of valor has come for you, and for no other man.

sanskrit: sa bhavān majjamānānāṃ bandhūnāṃ tvaṃ plavo yathā vividhāni tavāstrāṇi santi māyā ca rākṣasī
english: Be you, for your kinsmen who are sinking, like a raft; manifold are your weapons, and yours too is the magic of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: paśya karṇena haiḍimba pāṇḍavānām anīkinī kālyamānā yathā gāvaḥ pālena raṇamūrdhani
english: Behold, son of Hiḍimbā, the host of the Pāṇḍavas driven by Karṇa at the battle's front like cattle driven by a herdsman.

sanskrit: eṣa karṇo maheṣvāso matimān dṛḍhavikramaḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkeṣu nihanti kṣatriyarṣabhān
english: This Karṇa, the mighty archer, wise and firm in valor, slays the bulls among kṣatriyas within the Pāṇḍava ranks.

sanskrit: kirantaḥ śaravarṣāṇi mahānti dṛḍhadhanvinaḥ na śaknuvanty avasthātuṃ pīḍyamānāḥ śarārciṣā
english: Though they pour down great showers of arrows, the firm-bowed warriors cannot hold their ground, oppressed by the flame of his shafts.

sanskrit: niśīthe sūtaputreṇa śaravarṣeṇa pīḍitāḥ ete dravanti pāñcālāḥ siṃhasyeva bhayān mṛgāḥ
english: Tormented at midnight by the sūta's son with his rain of arrows, these Pāñcālas flee like deer from the terror of a lion.

sanskrit: etasyaivaṃ pravṛddhasya sūtaputrasya saṃyuge niṣeddhā vidyate nānyas tvad ṛte bhīmavikrama
english: Of this sūta's son, swollen so with might in combat, there is no other check save you, O you of fearsome valor.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ kuru mahābāho karma yuktam ihātmanaḥ mātulānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca tejaso 'strabalasya ca
english: So do you, mighty-armed one, perform here a deed worthy of yourself, of your maternal uncles and your fathers, of your splendor and the strength of your weapons.

sanskrit: etadarthaṃ hi haiḍimba putrān icchanti mānavāḥ kathaṃ nas tārayed duḥkhāt sa tvaṃ tāraya bāndhavān
english: For this very end, son of Hiḍimbā, do men desire sons—that one might deliver them from sorrow. Deliver, then, your kinsmen.

sanskrit: tava hy astrabalaṃ bhīmaṃ māyāś ca tava dustarāḥ saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya satataṃ bhīmanandana
english: For terrible is the strength of your weapons, and unmatchable your magic spells, ever as you fight in battle, O delight of Bhīma.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ prabhagnānāṃ karṇena śitasāyakaiḥ majjatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭreṣu bhava pāraṃ paraṃtapa
english: For the Pāṇḍavas, shattered by Karṇa's keen shafts and sinking amid the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, be the farther shore, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: rātrau hi rākṣasā bhūyo bhavanty amitavikramāḥ balavantaḥ sudurdharṣāḥ śūrā vikrāntacāriṇaḥ
english: For by night the rākṣasas grow yet more boundless in valor—strong, well-nigh invincible, heroic, and ranging in their might.

sanskrit: jahi karṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ niśīthe māyayā raṇe pārthā droṇaṃ vadhiṣyanti dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ
english: Slay Karṇa, the mighty archer, at midnight in battle by your magic; the Pārthas, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head, will slay Droṇa.

sanskrit: keśavasya vacaḥ śrutvā bībhatsur api rākṣasam abhyabhāṣata kauravya ghaṭotkacam ariṃdamam
english: Hearing the words of Keśava, Bībhatsu too, O scion of Kuru, addressed the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, tamer of foes.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaca bhavāṃś caiva dīrghabāhuś ca sātyakiḥ matau me sarvasainyeṣu bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Ghaṭotkaca, you yourself, and long-armed Sātyaki, and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava—these in my judgment are foremost among all our hosts.

sanskrit: sa bhavān yātu karṇena dvairathaṃ yudhyatāṃ niśi sātyakiḥ pṛṣṭhagopas te bhaviṣyati mahārathaḥ
english: Let you, then, go forth to fight a single-chariot duel with Karṇa this night; Sātyaki, the great car-warrior, shall be the guardian of your rear.

sanskrit: jahi karṇaṃ raṇe śūraṃ sātvatena sahāyavān yathendras tārakaṃ pūrvaṃ skandena saha jaghnivān
english: Slay the hero Karṇa in battle, aided by the Sātvata, as Indra of old slew Tāraka with Skanda at his side.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaca uvāca alam evāsmi karṇāya droṇāyālaṃ ca sattama anyeṣāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca kṛtāstrāṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: Ghaṭotkaca said: I am a match for Karṇa, O best of men, and a match for Droṇa too, and for the other high-souled kṣatriyas skilled in arms.

sanskrit: adya dāsyāmi saṃgrāmaṃ sūtaputrāya taṃ niśi yaṃ janāḥ saṃpravakṣyanti yāvad bhūmir dhariṣyati
english: This very night I shall give the sūta's son such a battle as men will tell of for as long as the earth endures.

sanskrit: na cātra śūrān mokṣyāmi na bhītān na kṛtāñjalīn sarvān eva vadhiṣyāmi rākṣasaṃ dharmam āsthitaḥ
english: And here I shall spare neither the brave, nor the frightened, nor those who join their palms in surrender; all alike I shall slay, holding to the rākṣasa's code.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā mahābāhur haiḍimbaḥ paravīrahā abhyayāt tumule karṇaṃ tava sainyaṃ vibhīṣayan
english: Saṃjaya said: Having so spoken, the mighty-armed son of Hiḍimbā, slayer of hostile heroes, advanced upon Karṇa in the tumult, striking terror into your army.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃkruddhaṃ dīptāsyam iva pannagam abhyasyan parameṣvāsaḥ pratijagrāha sūtajaḥ
english: As he rushed on in fury, like a serpent of blazing maw, the supreme archer, the sūta's son, met him with arrows and received his onset.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ karṇarākṣasayor niśi garjato rājaśārdūla śakraprahrādayor iva
english: Then there arose between those two, Karṇa and the rākṣasa, a roaring battle in the night, O tiger among kings, like that between Śakra and Prahrāda.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā ghaṭotkacaṃ rājan sūtaputrarathaṃ prati prayāntaṃ tvararyā yuktaṃ jighāṃsuṃ karṇam āhave
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Ghaṭotkaca, O king, advance with hot haste toward the chariot of the sūta's son, eager to slay Karṇa in the fray—

sanskrit: abravīt tava putras tu duḥśāsanam idaṃ vacaḥ etad rakṣo raṇe tūrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇasya vikramam
english: your son spoke these words to Duḥśāsana: This rākṣasa, beholding Karṇa's prowess, comes swiftly on in battle.

sanskrit: abhiyāti drutaṃ karṇaṃ tad vāraya mahāratham vṛtaḥ sainyena mahatā yāhi yatra mahābalaḥ
english: He rushes upon Karṇa—ward off that great car-warrior. Go, surrounded by a mighty force, to where the strong one stands.

sanskrit: karṇo vaikartano yuddhe rākṣasena yuyutsati rakṣa karṇaṃ raṇe yatto vṛtaḥ sainyena mānada
english: Karṇa Vaikartana means to do battle with the rākṣasa; guard Karṇa in the fight, ever watchful and ringed about with troops, O giver of honor.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rājañ jaṭāsurasuto balī duryodhanam upāgamya prāha praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: Meanwhile, O king, the mighty son of Jaṭāsura, foremost of those who strike, came to Duryodhana and spoke.

sanskrit: duryodhana tavāmitrān prakhyātān yuddhadurmadān pāṇḍavān hantum icchāmi tvayājñaptaḥ sahānugān
english: Duryodhana, your foes the Pāṇḍavas, renowned and maddened in war, I wish to slay with their followers, if you but command me.

sanskrit: jaṭāsuro mama pitā rakṣasām agraṇīḥ purā prayujya karma rakṣoghnaṃ kṣudraiḥ pārthair nipātitaḥ tasyāpacitim icchāmi tvaddiṣṭo gantum īśvara
english: Jaṭāsura, my father, foremost of rākṣasas, was of old struck down by the base Pārthas, who worked a rite to slay rākṣasas. I wish to avenge him; with your leave, lord, let me go.

sanskrit: tam abravīt tato rājā prīyamāṇaḥ punaḥ punaḥ droṇakarṇādibhiḥ sārdhaṃ paryāpto 'haṃ dviṣadvadhe tvaṃ tu gaccha mayājñapto jahi yuddhaṃ ghaṭotkacam
english: Then the king, well pleased, said to him again and again: With Droṇa, Karṇa, and the rest at my side, I am equal to the slaying of foes; but go you, at my command, and conquer Ghaṭotkaca in battle.

sanskrit: tathety uktvā mahākāyaḥ samāhūya ghaṭotkacam jaṭāsurir bhaimaseniṃ nānāśastrair avākirat
english: Saying "So be it," the huge-bodied son of Jaṭāsura challenged Ghaṭotkaca and covered the son of Bhīmasena with weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: alaṃbalaṃ ca karṇaṃ ca kurusainyaṃ ca dustaram haiḍimbaḥ pramamāthaiko mahāvāto 'mbudān iva
english: Alaṃbala and Karṇa and the unassailable host of the Kurus the son of Hiḍimbā churned single-handed, as a great gale churns the rain-clouds.

sanskrit: tato māyāmayaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathaṃ tūrṇam alaṃbalaḥ ghaṭotkacaṃ śaravrātair nānāliṅgaiḥ samārdayat
english: Then Alaṃbala, swiftly marking the chariot wrought of illusion, assailed Ghaṭotkaca with showers of arrows of every fashion.

sanskrit: viddhvā ca bahubhir bāṇair bhaimasenim alaṃbalaḥ vyadrāvayac charavrātaiḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: And having pierced the son of Bhīmasena with many shafts, Alaṃbala scattered the host of the Pāṇḍavas with his floods of arrows.

sanskrit: tena vidrāvyamāṇāni pāṇḍusainyāni māriṣa niśīthe viprakīryanta vātanunnā ghanā iva
english: Driven before him, O sir, the armies of the Pāṇḍavas were scattered abroad at midnight like clouds dispersed by the wind.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacaśarair nunnā tathaiva kuruvāhinī niśīthe prādravad rājann utsṛjyolkāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Likewise the host of the Kurus, driven by Ghaṭotkaca's arrows, fled at midnight, O king, casting away their torches by the thousand.

sanskrit: alaṃbalas tataḥ kruddho bhaimaseniṃ mahāmṛdhe ājaghne niśitair bāṇais tottrair iva mahādvipam
english: Then Alaṃbala in wrath struck the son of Bhīmasena in that great affray with keen arrows, as one goads a great elephant with hooks.

sanskrit: tilaśas tasya tad yānaṃ sūtaṃ sarvāyudhāni ca ghaṭotkacaḥ praciccheda prāṇadac cātidāruṇam
english: His car, his driver, and all his weapons Ghaṭotkaca cut to fragments fine as sesame, and roared most terribly.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaṃ śaravrātaiḥ kurūn anyān sahasraśaḥ alaṃbalaṃ cābhyavarṣan megho merum ivācalam
english: Then he rained his floods of arrows upon Karṇa, upon the other Kurus by the thousand, and upon Alaṃbala, as a cloud pours upon the unmoving Meru.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃcukṣubhe sainyaṃ kurūṇāṃ rākṣasārditam upary upari cānyonyaṃ caturaṅgaṃ mamarda ha
english: Then the army of the Kurus, harried by the rākṣasa, was thrown into turmoil, and the fourfold host crushed one another, rank upon rank.

sanskrit: jaṭāsurir mahārāja viratho hatasārathiḥ ghaṭotkacaṃ raṇe kruddho muṣṭinābhyahanad dṛḍham
english: The son of Jaṭāsura, O great king, his chariot lost and his driver slain, in fury smote Ghaṭotkaca hard in the battle with his fist.

sanskrit: muṣṭinābhihatas tena pracacāla ghaṭotkacaḥ kṣitikampe yathā śailaḥ savṛkṣagaṇagulmavān
english: Struck by that fist, Ghaṭotkaca reeled, as a mountain with its woods and thickets and clustered trees trembles in an earthquake.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa parighābhena dviṭsaṃghaghnena bāhunā jaṭāsuriṃ bhaimasenir avadhīn muṣṭinā bhṛśam
english: Then with his arm like an iron bludgeon, the bane of hosts of foes, the son of Bhīmasena smote the son of Jaṭāsura fiercely with his fist.

sanskrit: taṃ pramathya tataḥ kruddhas tūrṇaṃ haiḍimbir ākṣipat dorbhyām indradhvajābhābhyāṃ niṣpipeṣa mahītale
english: Having crushed him, the son of Hiḍimbā in wrath seized him swiftly and with arms like Indra's banner-staffs dashed him down upon the earth.

sanskrit: alaṃbalo 'pi vikṣipya samutkṣipya ca rākṣasam ghaṭotkacaṃ raṇe roṣān niṣpipeṣa mahītale
english: Alaṃbala in turn flung the rākṣasa off, then lifted Ghaṭotkaca high and in rage dashed him too down upon the earth.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ garjator atikāyayoḥ ghaṭotkacālaṃbalayos tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: Then there arose between those two roaring giants, Ghaṭotkaca and Alaṃbala, a tumultuous battle that made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: viśeṣayantāv anyonyaṃ māyābhir atimāyinau yuyudhāte mahāvīryāv indravairocanāv iva
english: Each surpassing the other, those two masters of illusion fought with their spells, mighty in valor, like Indra and the son of Virocana.

sanskrit: pāvakāmbunidhī bhūtvā punar garuḍatakṣakau punar meghamahāvātau punar vajramahācalau punaḥ kuñjaraśārdūlau punaḥ svarbhānubhāskarau
english: Becoming now fire and ocean, now Garuḍa and Takṣaka, now cloud and great wind, now thunderbolt and great mountain, now elephant and tiger, now Svarbhānu and the sun—

sanskrit: evaṃ māyāśatasṛjāv anyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇau bhṛśaṃ citram ayudhyetām alaṃbalaghaṭotkacau
english: thus conjuring a hundred illusions, each longing to slay the other, Alaṃbala and Ghaṭotkaca fought on in marvelous fashion.

sanskrit: parighaiś ca gadābhiś ca prāsamudgarapaṭṭiśaiḥ musalaiḥ parvatāgraiś ca tāv anyonyaṃ nijaghnatuḥ
english: With iron bars and maces, with darts and mallets and lances, with clubs and mountain-peaks, they smote each other.

sanskrit: hayābhyāṃ ca gajābhyāṃ ca padātirathinau punaḥ yuyudhāte mahāmāyau rākṣasapravarau yudhi
english: Now with horses, now with elephants, now on foot, now from chariots, those two foremost rākṣasas, great masters of magic, did battle in the fray.

sanskrit: tato ghaṭotkaco rājann alaṃbalavadhepsayā utpapāta bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ śyenavan nipapāta ha
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, O king, longing to slay Alaṃbala and exceedingly wrathful, sprang up and swooped down upon him like a hawk.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā ca mahākāyaṃ rākṣasendram alaṃbalam udyamya nyavadhīd bhūmau mayaṃ viṣṇur ivāhave
english: And seizing that huge-bodied lord of rākṣasas, Alaṃbala, he raised him aloft and dashed him to the ground, as Viṣṇu in battle slew Maya.

sanskrit: tato ghaṭotkacaḥ khaḍgam udgṛhyādbhutadarśanam cakarta kāyād dhi śiro bhīmaṃ vikṛtadarśanam
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, taking up a sword of wondrous aspect, severed from the trunk the dreadful, hideous-looking head.

sanskrit: tacchiro rudhirābhyaktaṃ gṛhya keśeṣu rākṣasaḥ ghaṭotkaco yayāv āśu duryodhanarathaṃ prati
english: Grasping that blood-smeared head by the hair, the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca went swiftly toward Duryodhana's chariot.

sanskrit: abhyetya ca mahābāhuḥ smayamānaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ rathe 'sya nikṣipya śiro vikṛtānanamūrdhajam prāṇadad bhairavaṃ nādaṃ prāvṛṣīva balāhakaḥ
english: Drawing near, the mighty-armed rākṣasa, smiling, cast onto his chariot the head with its disfigured face and hair, and uttered a fearful cry like a thunder-cloud in the rains.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tato rājan duryodhanam idaṃ vacaḥ eṣa te nihato bandhus tvayā dṛṣṭo 'sya vikramaḥ punar draṣṭāsi karṇasya niṣṭhām etāṃ tathātmanaḥ
english: And then, O king, he spoke these words to Duryodhana: Here is your ally slain; his valor you have seen. Soon you shall see this same end fall upon Karṇa—and upon yourself as well.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ prāyāt karṇaṃ prati janeśvara kirañ śaraśatāṃs tīkṣṇān vimuñcan karṇamūrdhani
english: Having so spoken, he then advanced toward Karṇa, O lord of men, pouring forth hundreds of sharp arrows and loosing them upon Karṇa's head.
